extracted.intended_audience: War Department legal officers, comptrollers, quartermaster and subsistence accountants, and other government appropriation/finance officials
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria for determining whether particular expenses may be charged to specified Army and related appropriations (e.g., contingencies, barracks and quarters, post exchanges, fortifications, hospitals, printing, etc.). Includes examples, statutory limits, and procedural directions for charging, apportioning, or certifying claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of appropriation language (shelter, shooting galleries, ranges, repairs)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriation 'for shelter, shooting galleries, ranges, repairs, and expenses incident thereto' is intended for target practice with small arms and does not cover the rental of a piece of ground for artillery practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small short-term rentals (occupation of the ground for a few days only), being of small amount, may properly be considered a legitimate charge against the appropriation for contingencies of the Army. Use the specific statutory language to determine intended equipment/use; do not expand a narrowly worded appropriation to unrelated heavy-arms uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingencies appropriation cannot supplement specific appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriation for contingencies of the Army is to meet necessary and appropriate expenses in connection with the Army 'not otherwise provided for,' and therefore is not available to supplement a specific appropriation for furnishing certain supplies or rendering certain services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a specific appropriation (e.g., repairs to a named building) is insufficient, the contingencies appropriation should not be used to cover the deficiency. Presenting claims should follow procedures for deficiency acts rather than charging contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment limits established by appropriation are binding
rubrics_metrics.description: An act appropriating salaries for a specified number of clerks (e.g., 'not exceeding 125 clerks') amounts to a provision of law that no more than that number should be employed on the work specified in the act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment or payment of workers in excess of the authorized number is prohibited from that appropriation and such excess personnel cannot be paid from the contingencies fund; ensure authorized headcounts are not exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army appropriations generally cover military-related persons/activities only
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenditures for medical treatment or burial of civilian employees injured while engaged in non-military work are not chargeable against the appropriation for contingencies of the Army, since that appropriation is for 'all branches of the military service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between military and civilian activities/personnel when allocating charges. Burial/medical expenses for civilians not in military service should not be charged to Army appropriations unless other law permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: No payment of tort damages from contingencies when U.S. not legally responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the United States is not legally responsible for the torts of its officers or agents, the Secretary of War cannot authorize from the appropriation for 'all contingent expenses of the Army not otherwise provided for' the payment of damages as compensation for personal injury to private persons in such circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use contingencies to pay tort damages absent statutory authorization; seek other remedies or Congressional appropriation if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory prohibitions override appropriation flexibility (clerical compensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of copyists employed in War Department bureaus out of the appropriation for Army contingencies would be an expenditure for clerical compensation and is prohibited by statute (sec. 3682 R.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always check for express statutory prohibitions (e.g., on clerical pay) before charging an expense to a given appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionable fit of non-military transactional expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: It is questionable whether the expense of selling a portion of a military reservation under an act of Congress can be regarded as an expense pertaining to the Army within the meaning of the appropriation 'for all contingent expenses of the Army.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt about whether a transactional expense (e.g., sale of land) is an Army expense, obtain legal guidance rather than presumptively charging contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts-martial appropriation covers witnesses' expenses necessary to prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriation for 'expenses of courts-martial and courts of inquiry and compensation of witnesses' may properly pay costs of witnesses (including railroad tickets for indigent witnesses), certified copies of evidentiary documents, transcripts, and fees necessary for prosecution before courts-martial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record amounts paid on witness vouchers for later deduction in settlements; ensure expenditures are necessary to prosecution. The appropriation has been applied to reporters for retiring boards and to fees of notaries for necessary swearing of witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on who is covered by 'compensation of witnesses'
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriation for compensation of witnesses has been held to refer to compensation of civilian witnesses only and not to apply to retired officers of the Army ordered to appear as witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not charge retired officers' appearance fees to the 'compensation of witnesses' appropriation unless statutory authority indicates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees of civil officials serving process generally not chargeable
rubrics_metrics.description: Although a summons or subpoena may legally be served by military or civil persons, there is no express authority for employment of a U.S. marshal or other civil official for serving process; the fees or expenses of such a person would not be a proper charge against the courts-martial appropriation unless service could not be otherwise made so effectually and economically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only pay fees of civil process servers from Army appropriations in exceptional circumstances where no practicable military alternative exists and reasonable compensation is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity limitation for inter-service court witness expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenses of a witness belonging to the Navy or Marine Corps attending an Army court-martial is a proper charge against the Army appropriation; conversely, the expense of a witness belonging to the Army attending a naval court-martial is not a charge against any Army appropriation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge witness expenses to the appropriation of the service convening the court; do not shift costs across services absent authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'telegrams on official business'
rubrics_metrics.description: Telegrams containing applications for leaves of absence, extensions, and inquiries as to whether leaves have been granted are not 'telegrams on official business' and cannot be paid from the appropriation for 'cost of telegrams on official business.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish personal leave applications from communications sent in the interest of service; where a telegram is sent by an officer in conduct of official duties (e.g., to relieve a hospital by enabling convalescents to go home), it may be treated as official and charged accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context can make otherwise-personal telegrams 'official'
rubrics_metrics.description: Telegrams requesting extension of a sick leave or sent to secure necessary retention of personnel for hospital interests have been held to be on official business and payable from official telegram appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate telegrams by purpose and effect on military service operations; when sent to further the interests of the service they may be charged to official telegram appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'barracks and quarters' — broad for necessary post buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'barracks and quarters' should not be restricted to company barracks and officers' quarters only; it may cover other buildings necessary to the administration of a military post (guardhouse, hospital, headquarters, post exchange, blacksmith and carpenter shops, pump house separated from main post, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construing 'barracks and quarters' broadly allows purchase of sites or construction for necessary incidental post buildings; however, certain structures (e.g., chapels) have been held not to be covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philippine 'proper shelter and protection' interpreted broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriation language for 'proper shelter and protection' of officers and enlisted men in the Philippine Islands includes hospitals, guardhouses, and storehouses in addition to living accommodations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriation language is broader than a literal reading, incidental structures necessary to shelter/protect troops may be charged to the appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of permanent buildings under annual 'barracks' appropriation — practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Although sec. 1136 R.S. requires detailed estimates and special appropriation for permanent barracks or quarters exceeding $20,000, practice has permitted construction of permanent buildings out of annual 'barracks and quarters' appropriation at cost not exceeding $20,000 and even more than one such building at a post (aggregate may exceed $20,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow departmental practice unless Congress or courts require otherwise; consult legal counsel for ambiguous cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post exchange appropriation — broad but limited to buildings and enlisted men’s benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriation for post exchanges intended for 'construction, equipment, and maintenance of suitable buildings' should be liberally construed to cover fences, grandstands, seats, athletic fields, and apparatus for outdoor and indoor athletics, but not tents intended as movable equipment, nor consumable sports gear (e.g., polo balls), nor movable commercial equipment (safes, cash registers). Appropriation is to be expended for the exclusive benefit of enlisted men and not for officers' mess furniture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge expenses that are for permanent buildings or necessary facilities for post exchange use by enlisted men; do not charge commercial-equipment purchases or officer benefits to the appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fortifications appropriation covers incidental items useful to defense works
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriation for fortifications and other works of defense and 'for the protection, preservation, and repair of fortifications for which there may be no special appropriation available' is sufficient to cover repair of a sailboat useful for transporting materials or making inspections connected with fortifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items incidentally and directly useful to fortifications may be charged to fortifications; ensure the item's primary use relates to defense works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge land purchase to appropriation whose primary purpose it serves
rubrics_metrics.description: Land at Corregidor Island that was essential in connection with construction, use, and maintenance of batteries and other works of defense but not for shelter of men should be purchased from the appropriation for fortifications, not 'barracks and quarters.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate purchase of land or property to the appropriation most directly connected to its use (fortifications vs. barracks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation vs storage expense separation (searchlights)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriation 'for the purchase and installation of searchlights' does not cover storehouses for the safe-keeping and shelter of such searchlights; storehouses should be charged to Quartermaster appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between buying/installation of equipment and providing permanent storage or related facilities; charge each to the appropriation suited to its nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional charging of expenses (fuel, coal prospecting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenses to develop coal fields by prospecting and testing by drilling operations were chargeable against the appropriation for 'regular supplies' because that appropriation is charged with providing fuel for the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge expenses to the appropriation that aligns with the function/purpose of the expenditure (e.g., fuel acquisition to regular supplies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency fund for unforeseen contingencies has specific scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An emergency fund appropriated 'to meet unforeseen contingencies' is available for disaster relief (e.g., relief of cyclone sufferers) but has limits and may not be available to reimburse certain expenditures (e.g., embezzled company funds or transportation of civilians) without further Congressional action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use emergency funds for genuine unforeseen public emergencies; for questionable reimbursements seek Congressional appropriation or legal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation funds are not generally transferable between appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: A sum legally payable out of a specific appropriation cannot be transferred to the credit of another appropriation; however, the Secretary of War may direct the transfer of amounts for disbursement to the disbursing officer at the place where the work will be performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not re-designate or transfer appropriations to avoid statutory limits; internal administrative transfers for disbursement purposes may be made when authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims against exhausted appropriations must be certified for deficiency acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Legitimate accounts properly payable out of an appropriation which has been fully expended should be transmitted to the Treasury Department as 'claims to be certified to be due by the accounting officers under appropriations the balances of which have been exhausted' and then certified to Congress for appropriation in a deficiency act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed claims/certification procedure rather than making unauthorized charges to other appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary's discretion to re-designate receipts under statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Under sec. 4 of the act of June 16, 1890, moneys paid upon purchase of discharges shall be deposited to the credit of current appropriations 'to be indicated by the Secretary of War,' and the Secretary may change his designation from time to time in his judgment for the interests of the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretarial designation of credits may be altered for service benefit; document rationale for changes in designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment of costs between appropriations for mixed-use items
rubrics_metrics.description: Where machinery or other items have mixed uses (e.g., woodworking machinery at a military prison used both for construction work and for instructing prisoners in trades), the cost may be apportioned between the special fund for reconstruction and the appropriation for support of the Army as the Secretary of War deems just and equitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an expenditure serves multiple statutory purposes, apportion costs based on estimated relative uses and obtain appropriate approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prison laundering machinery charged to support appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: Machinery for laundering prisoners' clothes, being related to prisoners rather than to the prison structure itself, is a proper charge against appropriations for the support of the Army (e.g., 'Camp and garrison equipage' or 'incidental expenses').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whether an item is prisoner-support (charge to support) or structural (charge to construction) and select the appropriation accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing costs charged to the appropriation related to subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost of printing special forms ordered by the Secretary of War for Inspector General use may be charged to the printing appropriation of either the Quartermaster's or the Subsistence Department, depending on the subject and who ordered it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge printing to the appropriation most closely connected to the content/purpose of the printed matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible charging among related appropriations for necessary supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchase of specially ruled sheets necessary to carry into effect appropriations for armament, arming militia, or stationery for the War Department may be charged to any one of those appropriations; if one is depleted the cost can be charged against another related appropriation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For items legitimately usable under several appropriations, charge against the most appropriate one and, where necessary, against related appropriations if one is unduly depleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge according to primary purpose (instruction vs defensive equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a plant at an Artillery School might be part of the armament of fortifications or solely for instruction, it should be charged to the fortifications appropriation if it is part of the defensive equipment, but to the support of the school appropriation if needed chiefly for instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the primary purpose of an acquisition; charge to the appropriation that reflects the acquisition's dominant function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific statutory appropriation with defined purpose takes precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific appropriation (e.g., river and harbor act provision to remove obstructions) should be construed broadly for its remedial purpose and is the proper appropriation to charge for that purpose rather than a more general appropriation for operating canals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a specific statute appropriates funds for a defined remedial purpose, charge related expenses to that statute rather than to general operating appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation chargeable with import purchase also covers legally assessed duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriation that is chargeable with the purchase price of Government property imported into the Philippine Islands is also chargeable with the payment of customs duties and internal-revenue taxes legally assessed against the United States under the appropriation act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include incidental legally-assessed import duties/taxes as chargeable to the appropriation that finances the imported government property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge utility costs to appropriation by purpose of use (gas example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gas supplied to a commissary storehouse: if needed for heating or lighting the storehouse, charge Quartermaster's appropriation; if needed for testing and sampling subsistence stores, charge the Subsistence Department appropriation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate utility and operating costs to the appropriation whose subject-matter use the utility serves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital-specific equipment/operating costs charged to Medical appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenses connected with installation and operation of electric fans for a military hospital are not incident to lighting a military post and should be charged to the appropriation for the Medical and Hospital Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge equipment and operation expenses to medical/hospital appropriations when they are for hospital-specific needs rather than general post functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-preparation removal costs charged to building appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where removal of buildings under control of another department is necessary to prepare a site for erection of a hospital, the expense of removal should be charged against the appropriation for the construction of the hospital regardless of prior departmental control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge preparatory site work to the appropriation funding the new construction when the removal is necessary for that construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone/message costs charged to fund related to the article or service referenced
rubrics_metrics.description: Each telephone message by a hospital should be charged against the fund out of which the article to which the message referred was purchased: messages about the sick and hospital detachment charged to hospital funds, while messages about purchase of medicines or hospital property charged to Quartermaster's Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate telecommunication expenses to the appropriation that funds the subject matter of the communication.
